1: # Pathland Core Events
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core events** the Pathland protocol supports.
12: Events are the **raw inputs** a renderer reports about the user's interaction —
13: pointer motion, keys, value changes, text edits, scroll. Only the **core
14: events** are specified here; **gestures** (tap, long-press, drag, magnify,
15: rotate) are explicitly **out of scope** and are composed application-side from
16: the raw pointer events (see [Deferred: gestures](#deferred-gestures)).
17: 
18: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
19: - Modifiers (properties): [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
20: - Wire format: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
21: 
22: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
23: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
24: > defines the protocol contract only.
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Event model
29: 
30: Events flow **host → guest**. The renderer is the producer; the app/engine is
31: the consumer. Both directions of the protocol are binary and share the same
32: 16-byte opcode format; events are `EVENT`-category (0x03) opcodes.
33: 
34: ### Who emits what
35: 
36: - The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
37:   writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
38: - The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its
39:   bound `State` signals (which in turn re-emit `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`
40:   deltas).
41: - The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
42:   wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
43:   bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
44:   (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.
45: 
46: ### Transport-aware event guards (MUST)
47: 
48: Renderers **MUST** implement event guards to prevent network noise. A user
49: interaction — tap, text change, drag, value edit — **MUST NEVER** produce an
50: outbound event opcode unless the target node explicitly declared intent in **at
51: least one** of these ways:
52: 
53: 1. it set the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) bits, **or**
54: 2. it is a **value-bearing control** reporting by component type (`SLIDER`,
55:    `TOGGLE`, `PICKER`, `MENU`, `DATE_PICKER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, …), **or**
56: 3. it carries a bound callback property — `ACTION_ID` (0x2016) or `BINDING_ID`
57:    (0x2017) — that identifies where the interaction must be routed.
58: 
59: Interactions that match none of these are **dropped at the renderer**; they are
60: never serialized to the event ring or a network batch. This is the wire-level
61: guard: a `Button` tap with no `ACTION_ID`, no `BINDING_ID`, and no
62: `EVENT_LISTENERS` produces no events.
63: 
64: ### Target resolution
65: 
66: The renderer resolves `targetId` from its own rendered-output tree (its
67: `id → native element` map): the event's position is hit-tested against that
68: tree to find the deepest node with the matching listener bit. If no listener is
69: declared, the event is not reported.
70: 
71: ### Transport paths
72: 
73: | Path | Mechanism |
74: |------|-----------|
75: | Shared memory (desktop/native) | The host writes `EVENT` opcodes into the event ring (host → guest) at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains at `eventReadCursor`. Events are consumed as written (no frame batching). |
76: | Network batch (SSR → browser) | Host → guest batches use the `0x0001` direction flag of the `PLPL` batch format (see OPCODE.md Transport) |
77: 
78: ### Encoding
79: 
80: Every event is a 16-byte opcode:
81: 
82: ```
83: [Category=0x03][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
84: ```
85: 
86: `TEXT_CHANGED` is the exception: its payload is an offset into the host → guest
87: event arena (shared memory) or the batch's string section (network), so it is
88: only fully decodable with that string source (the same convention as
89: `STYLE::SET_TEXT`).
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## Core event catalog
94: 
95: ### Pointer
96: 
97: Pointer events carry a viewport-relative point in **logical points** (`B`=x,
98: `C`=y, f32).
99: 
100: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
101: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
102: | `POINTER_DOWN` | 0x01 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | press (basis of `onTapGesture`, `Button` action) |
103: | `POINTER_MOVE` | 0x02 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` (0x0001) / `HOVER_LEAVE` (0x0002) | hover/enter/leave, drag basis |
104: | `POINTER_UP` | 0x03 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | release (basis of `onTapGesture`) |
105: 
106: - **Flags**:
107:   - `POINTER_SECONDARY`: the secondary button (right mouse, long-press) rather
108:     than the primary.
109:   - `HOVER_ENTER` (bit 0 of `POINTER_MOVE`): the pointer just entered the
110:     node's bounds (is now hovering). `HOVER_LEAVE` (bit 1): the pointer just
111:     left. A plain move has neither bit set.
112: - **Listener bits**: `POINTER_DOWN` (bit 0), `POINTER_MOVE` (bit 1),
113:   `POINTER_UP` (bit 2).
114: - **Renderer**: attaches native press/hover recognition to the matching native
115:   element when the listener bit is set. Multiple pointer events may be reported
116:   for one physical gesture (down → several moves → up), all for the same
117:   `targetId` while the pointer stays over the node.
118: 
119: ### Keyboard
120: 
121: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
122: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
123: | `KEY_DOWN` | 0x04 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` (0x0002) | `onKeyPress(.down)` |
124: | `KEY_UP` | 0x05 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | `onKeyPress(.up)` |
125: 
126: - **`keyCode`**: a **canonical, platform-independent logical key code** (a
127:   renderer maps native scancodes/key-codes onto this canonical set). The
128:   canonical set (letters/digits/arrows/Enter/Tab/…) is renderer-shared and
129:   documented in the conformance vectors.
130: - **`modifiers`**: u8 bitmask — `Shift`=0x01, `Control`=0x02, `Alt`=0x04,
131:   `Meta/Super`=0x08.
132: - **`KEY_REPEAT`**: bit 1 of flags; set when the key is an OS auto-repeat.
133: - **Listener bits**: `KEY_DOWN` (bit 3), `KEY_UP` (bit 4).
134: - **Focus**: keyboard events are reported to the focused node (the node that
135:   most recently gained focus), or to the node that declared the listener and
136:   has keyboard focus. See `FOCUS_CHANGED` below.
137: 
138: ### Value
139: 
140: Value events carry a control's semantic value, resolved by the renderer from
141: its own native control geometry.
142: 
143: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
144: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
145: | `VALUE_CHANGED` | 0x06 | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`Toggle`/`Picker`/`Menu` binding changes |
146: 
147: - **Semantics per control** (see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) controls):
148:   - `SLIDER`/`STEPPER`/`GAUGE` — the numeric value in the control's range.
149:   - `TOGGLE` — 0/1 (checked state; the same value the app writes to
150:     `SELECTED`).
151:   - `PICKER`/`MENU` — the selected option/action-item index.
152:   - `COLOR_PICKER` — the packed `0xAARRGGBB` color reinterpreted as an f32 bit
153:     pattern.
154:   - `DATE_PICKER` uses the dedicated `DATE_CHANGED` event below (its value is
155:     two fields and does not fit `VALUE_CHANGED`).
156: - The app writes the received value into its bound `State`; the engine's
157:   signal flush re-emits the `SET_PROPERTY` delta back to the renderer (the
158:   renderer reflects its own native control).
159: - **No listener bit**: value-bearing controls are reported by the renderer by
160:   virtue of their component type, but still gated by the transport-aware event
161:   guards (a control without `BINDING_ID` reports nothing). The renderer owns
162:   the gesture (e.g. slider drag) that produces them.
163: 
164: ### Date
165: 
166: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
167: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
168: | `DATE_CHANGED` | 0x0D | targetId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | `DatePicker` value binding |
169: 
170: - The date is encoded as two 32-bit fields — `B` = **days since epoch**
171:   (signed I32; pre-1970 is negative) and `C` = **millis of day** (U32,
172:   0..86,400,000) — matching the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (OPCODE.md). No
173:   string/arena indirection: the event is fully inline. It works over the
174:   shared-memory ring today and will use the same inline encoding for host →
175:   guest network batches once that direction lands (see OPCODE.md Transport).
176: - **No listener bit**: like `VALUE_CHANGED`, reported by virtue of the
177:   component type.
178: 
179: ### Text
180: 
181: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
182: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
183: | `TEXT_CHANGED` | 0x07 | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | `TextField` value binding |
184: | `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 0x08 | targetId | focused (0/1) | 0 | — | `@FocusState` |
185: | `EDITING_CHANGED` | 0x09 | targetId | editing (0/1) | 0 | — | `TextField`/`Slider` `onEditingChanged` |
186: | `SUBMIT` | 0x0A | targetId | 0 | 0 | — | `TextField` `onSubmit` / `onCommit` |
187: 
188: - **`TEXT_CHANGED`**: the new text is a length-prefixed entry
189:   (`[u32 byteLength][bytes…]`). Over the **shared-memory ring** the renderer
190:   bump-allocates it into the host-owned **event arena** and `B` is its absolute
191:   offset (see OPCODE.md); over the **network** it lives in the batch's string
192:   section referenced by a *relative* `B` offset — exactly the `STYLE::SET_TEXT`
193:   dual convention. A bare opcode cannot resolve the text; batch-aware decoders
194:   (`pathland-core-transport`, Java `FrameCodec`, TS `decoder.ts`) resolve it.
195:   The event is reported on **every** edit, including intermediate edits, not
196:   only on commit.
197: - **`FOCUS_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 gained focus, 0 lost focus. The renderer reports
198:   it for nodes that declared the `FOCUS` listener bit (bit 5). Focus is what
199:   routes subsequent `KEY_*` events.
200: - **`EDITING_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 editing session began, 0 ended. Reported for
201:   nodes that declared the `EDITING` listener bit (bit 6).
202: - **`SUBMIT`**: the user committed the field (Enter). Reported for nodes that
203:   declared the `SUBMIT` listener bit (bit 7). `B` MAY carry the current text as
204:   a string-section offset (reserved for future use; 0 today).
205: 
206: ### Scroll
207: 
208: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
209: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
210: | `SCROLL` | 0x0B | targetId | offsetX (f32) | offsetY (f32) | — | `ScrollView` offset, `onScrollPhaseChange` |
211: | `WHEEL` | 0x0C | targetId | deltaX (f32) | deltaY (f32) | — | `onScrollWheelEvent` / trackpad |
212: 
213: - **`SCROLL`**: the content offset of a `SCROLLVIEW` (logical points), reported
214:   for nodes that declared the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8). The renderer
215:   reports the absolute offset after each scroll delta.
216: - **`WHEEL`**: raw wheel/trackpad deltas (logical points), reported for nodes
217:   that declared the `WHEEL` listener bit (bit 9). Renderers map native scroll
218:   deltas (GTK `GtkEventControllerScroll`, DOM `wheel`) onto x/y deltas.
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: ## Event listeners (`EVENT_LISTENERS`)
223: 
224: `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) is a u32 bitmask set via `SET_PROPERTY` (U32). Each
225: bit requests one raw-input event kind for the node:
226: 
227: | Bit | Mask | Event |
228: | ----- | ------ | ------- |
229: | 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` |
230: | 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` (incl. hover enter/leave) |
231: | 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` |
232: | 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` |
233: | 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` |
234: | 5 | `0x00000020` | `FOCUS_CHANGED` |
235: | 6 | `0x00000040` | `EDITING_CHANGED` |
236: | 7 | `0x00000080` | `SUBMIT` |
237: | 8 | `0x00000100` | `SCROLL` |
238: | 9 | `0x00000200` | `WHEEL` |
239: | 10–31 | — | reserved |
240: 
241: Convenience aliases (DSL-side): `POINTER = bits 0|1|2`.
242: 
243: DSL surfaces:
244: 
245: - Rust: `pathland_view::pointer_events(mask)` modifier + `listener::*` bits;
246:   `on_tap_gesture` sets `POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_UP`.
247: - Java: `TapGestureView` / `EVENT_LISTENERS` via the emitter; host forwards raw
248:   `EVENT` batches into bound `State` signals.
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## Deferred: gestures
253: 
254: SwiftUI gestures — `onTapGesture`, `onLongPressGesture`, `DragGesture`,
255: `MagnifyGesture`, `RotateGesture` — are **not protocol events**. Per the
256: protocol's raw-inputs-only rule, they are **composed application-side** from
257: the raw `POINTER_*` / `KEY_*` events above:
258: 
259: - **Tap** = `POINTER_DOWN` then `POINTER_UP` on the same `targetId` within the
260:   platform's tap window.
261: - **Long-press** = `POINTER_DOWN` held past a threshold.
262: - **Drag** = `POINTER_DOWN` + `POINTER_MOVE` sequence.
263: - **Magnify / rotate** = multi-pointer deltas; the underlying raw events are
264:   `POINTER_*` (multi-touch reported per pointer).
265: 
266: A future "gesture recognition" layer MAY define app-side recognizers, but the
267: wire protocol will never carry interpreted gestures — only raw inputs.
268: 
269: ---
270: 
271: ## Reserved event command IDs
272: 
273: | Range | Use |
274: |-------|-----|
275: | `0x01`–`0x0D` | Core events (allocated, this file) |
276: | `0x0E`–`0x3F` | Future core events (unallocated) |
277: | `0x40`–`0xFF` | Custom/application events |
278: 
279: A renderer/decoder MUST skip unknown event commands and continue.
280: 
281: ---
282: 
283: ## Conformance
284: 
285: Event encode/decode round-trips and golden byte vectors (incl. raw-input
286: `EVENT` and network-batch bytes) live in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).
287: New events added here MUST add vectors before implementation.

(End of file - total 287 lines)
</content>

# pathland-view (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 25+ DSL (`com.pathland.view`):
SwiftUI-style views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
codec, lazy FFM ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Views**: `View` (open interface), `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Text`,
  `Image`, `Color` (dual identity: a `COLOR` view *and* a value passed into
  style modifiers), `Rectangle` (a `SHAPE` node), `Button`, `TextField`,
  `Spacer`; `body()` composition; `ButtonStyle`/`ViewModifier`/`Environment`
  (ScopedValue).
- **Component IDs**: synced to the spec's grouped ranges (`Components.java`:
  `TEXT 0x01`, `IMAGE 0x02`, `COLOR 0x03`, `SHAPE 0x04`, `SPACER 0x06`,
  `VSTACK 0x10`, `HSTACK 0x11`, `ZSTACK 0x12`, `BUTTON 0x20`, `TEXT_FIELD 0x21`,
  `TOGGLE 0x24`, `SLIDER 0x25`, `COMMENT 0x7F`, …) — frames are spec-valid and
  cross-language correct.
- **Modifiers**: `foregroundStyle(Color)` (no `.color()`), `background(Color)`,
  `tint(Color)`, padding/opacity/font/etc. — `Color` is never a modifier.
- **Value types**: `ValueTypes.forProperty` mirrors `value_type_for`
  (`VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` are `U8`); `FontWeight` uses the spec's
  numeric 100–900 scale.
- **Signals** (`com.pathland.view.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked` — glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression,
  circular-dependency detection.
- **Emitter** (`emit`): mounts once, stable ids, node-level binding effects
  (a signal change re-emits only that node), `FrameOpcodeSink` /
  `RingOpcodeSink`.
- **Wire codec** (`transport`): `FrameCodec` — self-contained `PLPL` frames
  both directions, `encodeEvents`/`decodeEvents` (host→guest events with
  `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section offsets).
- **FFM ring interop** (`ffm`): lazy `libpathland_core` binding, zero JNI.
- **State** (`state`): `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`, auto-wired by
  `pathland-view-processor`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Missing **modifiers/properties** (text-format, effects, transform, layout
  bounds, semantic extras) — see `spec/MODIFIERS.md`; the `View` chain surface
  covers only a subset.
- Missing **control views**: `Toggle`/`Slider`/`TextEditor`/`Picker`/
  `DatePicker`/`Menu`/`ColorPicker`/`Stepper`/`ProgressView`/`Gauge`/
  `Divider`/`Grid`/`ScrollView`/lazy stacks, and the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`
  helpers that route their events.
- Missing **events**: `FrameCodec.decodeEvents` decodes pointer +
  `VALUE_CHANGED` + `TEXT_CHANGED` only — no `KEY_*`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`,
  `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`; no
  `STYLE::SET_DATE` command; no arbitrary `EVENT_LISTENERS` modifier (only
  `TapGestureView`).
- `Truncation` has an extra `NONE` value not in the spec.

## Verified by

`mvn test` (needs JDK 25) — emitter, codec round-trips, signals, state.

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The **pure-function SSR HTML renderer** (`com.pathland.render.html`). Protocol
contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- Applies `Frame` deltas to a retained node map and renders HTML fragments /
  documents (`applyFrame`, `render`, `renderFragment`).

  `SLIDER`, `TEXT_FIELD`. Unknown components render their children.

  `MENU`, `COLOR_PICKER`.

  `pathland-render-html` (which is the fuller reference).

`mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — HTML renderer tests.

New view classes (each renders a PathlandNode with the correct component + properties + input wiring):

Properties: TOGGLE_STYLE (F32 enum float), SELECTED (U8 int), LABEL (STRING), BINDING_ID (U32). Event: VALUE_CHANGED (B=0/1) → valueInput writes `binding.set(value > 0)`. 
   Actually the emitter routes `VALUE_CHANGED` via `valueInputs` (Consumer<Float>). For Toggle, the value is 0/1 as f32. The app-side consumer: `value -> binding.set(value > 0)`. But the spec says VALUE_CHANGED with B = 0/1; a bool binding. The host routes valueInputs. So Toggle exposes `node.valueInput = v -> binding.set(v > 0f)`.

2. **Slider** — `SLIDER` (0x25). ctor `Slider(float value, float min, float max, WritableSignal<Float> binding)`. Properties: VALUE, MIN_VALUE, MAX_VALUE (F32). Event VALUE_CHANGED → valueInput sets binding directly.

3. **Stepper** — `STEPPER` (0x26). ctor `Stepper(float value, float min, float max, float step, WritableSignal<Float> binding)`. Properties VALUE/MIN/MAX/STEP_VALUE.

TextEditor multi-line: content via SET_TEXT, value binding via BINDING_ID. It's basically TextField without prompt. I'll mirror TextField.

5. **DatePicker** — `DATE_PICKER` (0x27). ctor `DatePicker(DatePickerMode mode, int daysSinceEpoch, int millisOfDay, WritableSignal<...>)`. The value is set via STYLE::SET_DATE command (which we're adding in Part B). This is more complex — the emitter/sink needs a setDate method. Hmm. For scope control, I could implement DatePicker minimal: render node with DATE_PICKER_MODE + BINDING_ID, and expose valueInput for DATE_CHANGED? The DATE_CHANGED event has B=days, C=millis. The valueInput is Consumer<Float> — doesn't carry two fields. This is getting complex.

For DatePicker, the SET_DATE command support requires adding to OpcodeSink interface + both sinks + Emitter + codec decode of DATE_CHANGED. That's a fair amount. But I can implement it.

47:         this.root = new CounterView();
48: 
49:         this.sink = new FrameOpcodeSink() {

51:             public void endFrame() {
52:                 super.endFrame();
53:                 Frame frame = frame();
54:                 if (!frame.opcodes().isEmpty()) {
55:                     html.applyFrame(frame);
56:                     WebSocketSession s = session;
57:                     if (s == null || !s.isOpen()) {
58:                         pending.add(frame);
59:                     } else {
60:                         send(frame);

63:             }

68:         RenderResult result = emitter.mount(root, new Environment(state));

71:         this.valueInputs = result.valueInputs();
72:         this.rootId = result.rootId();

## Part 1 — `pathland-demo-views` kitchensink

**New files** in `com.pathland.demo` (one custom `View` class per section, each with `State<T>` fields using explicit keys):

4. `TextFieldSection.java` — `State<String> name` ("name"), `TextField` + `TextEditor`, computed label.
5. `ToggleSection.java` — `State<Boolean>` ×3 (`dark`/`notify`/`bold`), all three `ToggleStyle`s (Switch/Checkbox/Button) + computed summary.
6. `ValueControlsSection.java` — `State<Float> value` ("value"), `Slider`, `Stepper`, `Gauge`, `ProgressView` all bound to it, computed label.

8. `ColorSection.java` — `State<Color> accent` ("accent"), `ColorPicker` + `Color` view swatch + `Rectangle`.
9. `DateSection.java` — `State<Integer> days` ("days"), `DatePicker`, computed date label.
10. `LayoutSection.java` — `Grid`, `LazyVStack`, `HStack`+`Spacer`, `ZStack` badge, `Divider`.
11. `TextStylesSection.java` — one `Text` row per modifier (fontWeight/italic/underline/strikethrough/textCase/kerning/tracking/lineLimit/fontDesign).
12. `AppearanceSection.java` — `border`/`shadow`/`opacity`/`clipped`/`clipShape`/`rotation`/`scaleEffect`/`zIndex` on a styled card.

# pathland-demo-views — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The framework-agnostic shared demo views (`com.pathland.demo`), consumed by the
Quarkus and Spring Boot demos. Uses `State` fields wired by the
`pathland-view-processor` annotation processor.

## Implemented

- **`KitchenSinkView`** (the demo root): a scrollable column of every protocol
  section, mounted by both demos' `SessionApp`.
- **Sections** (each a custom `View`):
  - `SectionCard` — reusable titled/bordered/rounded section wrapper.
  - `CounterSection` — `State<Integer>` + `Button` + `Stepper`.
  - `TextFieldSection` — `TextField` + `TextEditor` on one `State<String>`.
  - `ToggleSection` — `Toggle` in all three `ToggleStyle`s.
  - `ValueControlsSection` — `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`ProgressView` on one
    `State<Float>`.
  - `PickerSection` — `Picker` (Segmented + Menu) + `Menu`.
  - `ColorSection` — `ColorPicker` + `Color` as a View + reactive `Rectangle`.
  - `DateSection` — `DatePicker` bound to days-since-epoch.
  - `LayoutSection` — `Grid`/`LazyVStack`/`HStack`+`Spacer`/`ZStack`/`Divider`.
  - `TextStylesSection` — text-formatting modifiers.
  - `AppearanceSection` — border/shadow/opacity/transform/hidden/z-index.
- **Legacy views kept**: `CounterView`, `CounterControls`, `NameField` (still
  covered by `CounterViewTest`).

## Not implemented / gaps

- The browser experience depends on the Angular renderer and the demos'
  `app.js`, which are synced separately (see `lib/angular` and the demo
  `src/main/resources`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views` (needs JDK 25) — `CounterViewTest`,
`KitchenSinkViewTest` (mount + persistence + input routing).

 * `pathland_core::constants` (see `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 * and `spec/OPCODE.md`). These IDs are part of the wire format and must not change.
 */
export const CATEGORY = {
  TREE: 0x01,
  STYLE: 0x02,
  EVENT: 0x03,
  META: 0x04,
} as const;

export const TREE = {
  CREATE_NODE: 0x01,
  DELETE_NODE: 0x02,
  INSERT_CHILD: 0x03,
  REMOVE_CHILD: 0x04,
  MOVE_CHILD: 0x05,
} as const;

export const STYLE = {
  SET_PROPERTY: 0x01,
  SET_DESIGN_TOKEN: 0x02,
  SET_TEXT: 0x03,
  SET_DATE: 0x04,
} as const;

export const EVENT = {
  POINTER_DOWN: 0x01,
  POINTER_MOVE: 0x02,
  POINTER_UP: 0x03,

# lib/angular — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The Angular 21 **browser renderer** mapping opcode frames onto the
`@apaq/ngui` design system (`ui-vstack`/`ui-text`/`ui-button`/…). Protocol
contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Protocol constants** (`core/protocol.ts`): synced to the spec's grouped
  component ranges (`TEXT 0x01`, `COLOR 0x03`, `VSTACK 0x10`, `HSTACK 0x11`,
  `TOGGLE 0x24`, `SLIDER 0x25`, `COMMENT 0x7F`, …), full property catalog
  (incl. `TINT`/`SHAPE_KIND`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`/`PICKER_STYLE`/`SELECTION`/
  `COLOR_VALUE`/`DATE_PICKER_MODE`/…), `STYLE::SET_DATE`, the full event
  catalog (`KEY_*`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`,
  `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`), listener bits 0–9, and `FONT_WEIGHT` on the spec's
  100–900 scale.
- **Decoder** (`core/decoder.ts`): `PLPL` batch decode (`decodeFrame`),
  `HOST_TO_GUEST` direction, `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section resolution.
- **Retained tree** (`core/retained-tree.ts`): applies `TREE`/`STYLE` deltas
  including `STYLE::SET_DATE` (node date state).
- **Event encoder** (`core/event-encoder.ts`): host→guest event batches —
  pointer, `VALUE_CHANGED` (f32 or raw bits), `TEXT_CHANGED` with string
  offsets, `DATE_CHANGED` (days/millis).
- **ngui mapping** (`ngui/mapping.ts`): all spec components — stacks (incl.
  `LAZY_*`), `ZSTACK`, `GRID`, `SCROLLVIEW`, `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `IMAGE`,
  `COLOR`, `SHAPE`, `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `TEXT_FIELD`, `TEXT_EDITOR`,
  `TOGGLE` (`TOGGLE_STYLE` → switch/checkbox/button), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`,
  `PICKER`, `MENU`, `COLOR_PICKER`, `DATE_PICKER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`, `GAUGE`;
  `hidden` reads the `VISIBLE` `U8` bit.
- **Renderer** (`ngui/node.component.ts|html`): one case per kind — ngui views
  for the supported ones, native HTML elements for the rest (textarea, select,
  color/date inputs, range, progress, gauge, stepper); input routed back as
  `VALUE_CHANGED`/`TEXT_CHANGED`/`DATE_CHANGED`.
- **Session** (`ngui/session.service.ts`): connects to `/ws`, the server
  replays the mount frame on connect (`SessionApp`).

## Not implemented / gaps

1: # Pathland Protocol
2: 
3: > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol inspired by SwiftUI
4: 
5: ## Overview
6: 
7: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
8: multiple renderer backends. It's inspired by SwiftUI's declarative syntax, but
9: designed to be **language-agnostic** and **platform-agnostic**.
10: 
11: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
12: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
13: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
14: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
15: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
16: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
17: 
18: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
19: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
20: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`).
21: 
22: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
23: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
24: change detection is fine-grained and signal-based — a signal bound to a node's
25: text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas, so only the things that
26: actually changed emit opcodes and an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
27: 
28: ## The Three Elements
29: 
30: Pathland is composed of three elements. They are the vocabulary the whole
31: project speaks, so they are settled and used consistently:
32: 
33: ```
34: ┌────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
35: │ 1. Retained UI     │        │ 3. Renderer         │
36: │ the app's UI tree  │────┐   │ maps opcodes onto   │
37: │ (any language,     │    │   │ native elements +   │
38: │  any platform)     │    │   │ event reporting     │
39: └────────────────────┘    │   └───────────▲─────────┘
40:                          │                │
41: ┌────────────────────┐    │                │
42: │ 2. Opcode engine   │◄───┘                │
43: │ reconciles + emits │─────────────────────┘
44: └────────────────────┘
45: ```
46: 
47: 1. **Retained UI** — the application's canonical retained UI tree. It is the
48:    single source of truth, owned by the application. It can be authored in
49:    **any language on any platform**: Rust, Java, Swift, C#, C, TypeScript —
50:    desktop, mobile, or embedded — through a generated DSL or the flat native C
51:    ABI.
52: 2. **Opcode engine** — the producer: reconciles the retained tree and emits it as
53:    fixed **16-byte opcodes** using fine-grained, signal-based change detection: a
54:    signal bound to a node's text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas,
55:    so only the things that actually changed emit and an unchanged tree emits zero
56:    opcodes. The engine is language-independent — the same opcode stream serves
57:    every renderer. It spans a pure protocol core (`pathland-core`) and a
58:    retained-tree emitter (`pathland-engine`).
59: 3. **Renderer** — consumes the opcode stream and maps it onto that platform's
60:    **native elements**, and reports raw inputs back as events. It is a pure
61:    function of the opcode stream (stateless) and never retains application
62:    state. *"Host" and "driver" are roles a renderer plays: it runs inside a
63:    host and is pumped by a driver — they are not separate elements.* The same
64:    opcode stream targets **different UI systems**: a GTK4 renderer on desktop,
65:    an AppKit/SwiftUI renderer on macOS, a WinUI renderer on Windows, an LVGL
66:    renderer on embedded, a DOM renderer in the browser.
67: 
68: The opcodes are carried from the engine to the renderer by a transport (a
69: zero-copy shared-memory ring on desktop/native, a serialized network batch for
70: remote/browser); transport is an implementation detail, not a fourth element.
71: 
72: ## Core Principles
73: 
74: - **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
75: - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
76: - **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
77: - **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
78: - **Reactive emission**: fine-grained, signal-based change detection — only the nodes that actually changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
79: - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
80: - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
81: - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
82: - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
83: - **Hand-written Java DSL**: the SwiftUI-like view DSL lives as a reusable Java library (`com.pathland.view`), not generated code — one ergonomic surface for desktop, server (Spring/Quarkus), and embedded hosts
84: 
85: ## Documentation
86: 
87: ### Specification
88: 
89: - [Opcode Protocol](./spec/OPCODE.md) — **Primary specification** — fixed 16-byte opcodes, ring buffer, arena, reactive emission, design tokens
90: - [Primitive Views](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md) — the primitive views the protocol supports (SwiftUI groupings), with protocol component IDs and status
91: - [Core Modifiers](./spec/MODIFIERS.md) — the core modifiers (protocol `STYLE` properties), SwiftUI-style, with property IDs and status
92: - [Core Events](./spec/EVENTS.md) — the core events (raw inputs), SwiftUI-style, with event command IDs and listener bits
93: - [Conformance Test Vectors](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte arrays for validating implementations
94: 
95: ## Rust Workspace
96: 
97: The implementation is under [`lib/rust/`](./lib/rust/):
98: 
99: | Crate | Element | Responsibility |
100: |-------|---------|----------------|
101: | `pathland-view` | Retained UI | SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + chainable modifiers building a `pathland-engine::Node` tree (`no_std`) |
102: | `pathland-core` | Opcode engine | Protocol core: fixed 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, events, memory layout, Guest/Host/Frame surface (`no_std`, zero-alloc) |
103: | `pathland-engine` | Opcode engine | Emitter: retained tree types (`Node`/`Component`) + diff-based reactive emission + reactive **signals** (moved out of `pathland-core`) |
104: | `pathland-core-transport` | Opcode engine | Transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode + batching policy (`std`) |
105: | `pathland-render-gtk` | Renderer | GTK4 renderer (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames → native GTK widgets, incrementally |
106: | `pathland-render-html` | Renderer | HTML renderer: maps opcode frames onto declarative HTML (flex stacks, spans, buttons) as a pure function of the stream — the server-side/remote target |
107: | `pathland-view-native` | Retained UI projection | Native C-ABI shim + `NativeHost`: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring (Swift/Java/C#…) |
108: | `pathland-core-capi` | Opcode engine | Minimal shared-memory ring C ABI (`libpathland_core`): create/destroy, ring push, frame boundaries, arena alloc, zero-copy read, event drain/send |
109: | `pathland-render-gtk-demo` | Demo | Rust GTK4 demo: authors the DSL, renders through `pathland-render-gtk` (no GTK APIs) |
110: 
111: ## Java Libraries
112: 
113: The reusable, framework-agnostic Java libraries live under [`lib/java/`](./lib/java/)
114: (Maven reactor, `org.pathland`, Java 25+):
115: 
116: | Module | Package | Responsibility |
117: |--------|---------|----------------|
118: | `pathland-view` | `com.pathland.view` | SwiftUI-like view DSL (`View`, `VStack`, `Text`, `Button`, …), Angular-style signals/computed/effects (`com.pathland.view.signal`), fine-grained opcode emitter (`com.pathland.view.emit`), wire codec (`com.pathland.view.transport`), lazy FFM ring interop (`com.pathland.view.ffm`), cross-platform state (`com.pathland.view.state`: `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`) |
119: | `pathland-view-processor` | `com.pathland.processor` | JSR 269 annotation processor: generates `<View>_StateBinder` for `State` fields (auto-keyed by field name) |
120: | `pathland-render-html` | `com.pathland.render.html` | Pure-function HTML renderer over the opcode stream (SSR) with `data-pathland-id` hydration |
121: | `pathland-state-redis` | `com.pathland.state.redis` | Redis-backed `StateStore` over Lettuce (Spring/Quarkus/desktop) |
122: | `pathland-demo-views` | `com.pathland.demo` | Shared demo views (`CounterView`/`CounterControls`/`NameField`) declaring `State` fields |
123: | `pathland-quarkus-demo` | `com.pathland.quarkus` | Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo consuming the libraries |
124: | `pathland-spring-boot-demo` | `com.pathland.spring` | Spring Boot SSR + WebSocket demo consuming the same libraries |
125: 
126: The same `com.pathland.view` DSL (and `State` fields) runs unchanged on a Spring Boot
127: app, a Quarkus app, or a desktop app; a desktop host pushes opcodes into the Rust ring via
128: FFM (`pathland_ring_buffer_push`), while a server emits self-contained frames over WebSocket.
129: 
130: ### Build & run the Java libraries
131: 
132: ```bash
133: # Rust ring C ABI (only needed for the desktop FFM path)
134: cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

157: 
158: ### Run tests
159: 
160: ```bash
161: cd lib/rust && cargo test

164: 
165: ### Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)
166:

168: cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo
169: ```
170: 
171: ## Angular Renderer (@apaq/ngui)
172: 
173: The browser also has a declarative renderer: an **Angular application** (under
174: [`lib/angular/`](./lib/angular/)) that maps the opcode stream onto the
175: **[@apaq/ngui](https://github.com/Apaq/ngui)** design system — `ui-vstack`/
176: `ui-hstack`/`ui-text`/`ui-button`/… views and `[padding]`/`[color]`/`[font]`/…
177: modifiers — instead of hand-written `app.js` DOM patches. It connects to the
178: Pathland `/ws` socket (the server replays the full mount frame on connect, so no
179: SSR pre-step is needed), decodes `PLPL` frames, and renders ngui views. See
180: [`lib/angular/README.md`](./lib/angular/README.md).
181: 
182: ## Components & Properties
183: 
184: Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-core`'s
185: [`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs),
186: documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md), and catalogued by category in
187: [PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md) (component types), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md)
188: (properties), and [EVENTS.md](./spec/EVENTS.md) (events). Component types
189: include `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `VSTACK`, `HSTACK`, `SPACER`, and more; stack
190: constraint properties (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling
191: modifiers (`PADDING`, `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and
192: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.
193: 
194: ## Design Tokens
195: 
196: The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
197: Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
198: referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with
199: `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).
200: 
201: ## Roadmap (POC Goals)
202: 
203: See the GitHub issues (#12, #13, #15, #16, #18):
204: 
205: 1. **16-byte opcode engine** — done

487: ## Design Token System
488: 
489: ### Core Principle
490: 
491: > **The renderer owns the defaults. The application owns the overrides.**
492: 
493: This ensures a native look-and-feel by default and cross-platform consistency when the application overrides tokens.
494: 
495: ### Responsibilities
496: 
497: | Aspect | Owner | Responsibility |
498: |--------|-------|----------------|
499: | **Default Token Values** | Renderer | Define platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens |
500: | **Token Overrides** | Application | Specify overrides for cross-platform consistency |
501: | **Token Resolution** | Renderer | Resolve final token values (override or default) |
502: | **Platform Adaptation** | Renderer | Adapt default token values to platform conventions |
503: 
504: ### Token Identification
505: 
506: Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`, `font.body`), case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. The `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) references a token path stored in the arena; `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides a token's value globally.
507: 
508: ### Token Resolution Algorithm
509: 
510: ```
511: FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath: string) -> PropertyValue:
512:     IF applicationOverrides.has(tokenPath):
513:         RETURN applicationOverrides[tokenPath]
514:     ELSE IF rendererDefaults.has(tokenPath):
515:         RETURN rendererDefaults[tokenPath]
516:     ELSE IF hasParentToken(tokenPath):
517:         RETURN resolveToken(getParentPath(tokenPath))
518:     ELSE:
519:         RETURN getFallbackValue(tokenPath)
520: ```
521: 
522: ### Renderer Responsibilities
523: 
524: The renderer MUST:
525: 
526: 1. Provide platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens (e.g. `color.primary`, `font.body.size`, `space.md`).
527: 2. Accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
528: 3. Resolve design-token references in properties.
529: 4. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
530: 5. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.
531: 
532: The application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` and reference tokens via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; it MUST NOT assume specific default token values.
533: 
534: ### Standard Token Catalog
535: 
536: Required core tokens (renderer MUST support with platform-appropriate defaults): `color.primary`, `color.secondary`, `color.background`, `color.surface`, `color.text.primary`, `color.text.secondary`, `color.border`, `font.body.size`, `font.body.weight`, `font.body.family`, `space.xs`–`space.lg`.

- **Renderer** (`ngui/node.component.ts|html`): one case per kind, using **only
  `@apaq/ngui` components** — stacks/grids/`ui-text`/`ui-button`/`ui-checkbox`/
  `ui-toggle`/`ui-text-field`/`ui-text-area`/`ui-select`/`ui-radio-group`/
  `ui-menu`/`ui-date-picker`/`ui-rectangle`/`ui-circle`. Protocol components the
  design system lacks render a temporary **"not implemented" placeholder**
  (`NotImplementedComponent`, ngui-styled): `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`,
  `PROGRESS_VIEW`, `GAUGE`, `COLOR_PICKER`, `DIVIDER`, `SecureField`,
  `PICKER::Wheel`, `DATE_PICKER::Time/DateAndTime`, `SHAPE::Path`.
- Input is routed back as `VALUE_CHANGED`/`TEXT_CHANGED`/`DATE_CHANGED`
  (toggle/checkbox/button, select/radio-group/segmented, menu, text-area,
  date-picker).
- **Session** (`ngui/session.service.ts`): connects to `/ws`, the server
  replays the mount frame on connect (`SessionApp`).

## Not implemented / gaps

- No `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` gating (the Java emitter routes by node id via
  `RenderResult` registries).
- Protocol components without an ngui equivalent render as "not implemented"
  placeholders (listed above) until the design system adds them.
- `app.spec.ts` is an `ng test` (Karma/Jasmine) spec; the unit specs
  (`core.spec.ts`, `mapping.spec.ts`) run under vitest.

Now P3 — modifiers mapped to ngui.

ngui modifier directives available (from the exports): `[underline]`, `[shadow]`, `[rotationEffect]`, `[font]`, `[frame]`, `[flex]`, `[padding]`, `[color]`, `[background]`, `[border]`, `[rounding]`, `[opacity]`, `[lineLimit]`, `[controlSize]`, `[foregroundStyle]`, `[a11y]`, `[cursor]`, `[animate]`, `[zlayer]`, `[focusable]`.

Mapping spec properties → ngui modifiers:
- FONT_STYLE (italic) → FontOptions.style = 'italic' (FontOptions has `style?: string`).
- LINE_SPACING → FontOptions.lineHeight = `{lineSpacing}px`.
- UNDERLINE → `[underline]` modifier! ngui has `[underline]` directive (Underline). What's its input type? Probably `UnderlineOptions` or a boolean. Let me check.
- STRIKETHROUGH → ngui? No strikethrough modifier. `[underline]` only. So STRIKETHROUGH not directly mappable → could approximate via... no ngui strikethrough. Skip (not mapped) — it's a gap but ngui doesn't have it. The user's P3 scope said "text-format (italic/underline/strikethrough/textCase/kerning/tracking/lineSpacing)". textCase/kerning/tracking/strikethrough aren't ngui modifiers. Hmm.
  - textCase → no ngui modifier. Skip.
  - kerning → FontOptions? FontOptions has family/size/weight/style/lineHeight. No kerning. Skip.
  - tracking → no. Skip.
  - strikethrough → no. Skip.
  So P3 can map what ngui supports: FONT_STYLE→style, LINE_SPACING→lineHeight, UNDERLINE→[underline]. The rest remain unmapped (ngui doesn't provide them). That's acceptable — the renderer can only map to ngui's surface. I'll document.
- frame min/ideal/max → FrameOptions has minWidth/minHeight/maxWidth/maxHeight. Map MIN_WIDTH→minWidth, MAX_WIDTH→maxWidth, MIN_HEIGHT→minHeight, MAX_HEIGHT→maxHeight. IDEAL_* → no direct map (skip or map to width?). FrameOptions has no ideal. Skip ideal.
- frame alignment → FrameOptions.alignment (NguiAlignment). Map ALIGNMENT property on frame to frame.alignment. But ALIGNMENT (0x0002) is also the stack alignment. For the frame modifier, SwiftUI's frame(width:height:alignment:) sets ALIGNMENT. In our DSL, `.frame(width,height,alignment)` sets WIDTH/HEIGHT/ALIGNMENT. So when building frame for a leaf, ALIGNMENT could map to frame.alignment. But careful: buildFrame is called for all nodes; a stack's ALIGNMENT shouldn't become frame.alignment. Hmm. The frame modifier emits ALIGNMENT but so does a stack constructor. There's ambiguity. SwiftUI frame alignment only matters when width/height present. Let me map frame.alignment only when WIDTH or HEIGHT is set AND ALIGNMENT present: `if ((width || height) && alignment) frame.alignment = nguiAlignment(alignment)`.
- effects/transform:
  - SHADOW → `[shadow]` modifier! ngui has `[shadow]` (Shadow). ShadowOptions — check type. Map SHADOW_COLOR/RADIUS/X/Y → shadow options.
  - ROTATION_DEGREES → `[rotationEffect]` modifier! RotationOptions `{ angle }`? Check.
  - SCALE → `[scale]`? ngui doesn't export a scale modifier. No scale. Skip.
  - BLUR/SATURATION/etc → no ngui filter modifiers (BackgroundOptions has `filter?: string`! The Background modifier accepts a `filter`). So BLUR_RADIUS/SATURATION/etc → background.filter CSS string. That's a nice mapping: `[background]="{ filter: 'blur(4px)' }"`. But background already used for BACKGROUND_COLOR. The Background modifier input has both `color` and `filter`. So combine: if BACKGROUND_COLOR present → color; if BLUR etc → filter. Build a `backgroundFilter(node)` combining blur/saturation/contrast/brightness/grayscale/hue-rotate. Let me map:
    - BLUR_RADIUS → `blur({{r}}px)`
    - SATURATION → `saturate({{s}})`
    - CONTRAST → `contrast({{c}})`
    - BRIGHTNESS → `brightness({{b}})`
    - GRAYSCALE → `grayscale({{g}})`
    - HUE_ROTATION → `hue-rotate({{h}}deg)`
    - COLOR_MULTIPLY/COLOR_INVERT → not CSS filter directly (invert is `invert(1)`). COLOR_INVERT → `invert(1)`. COLOR_MULTIPLY → `sepia(1) hue-rotate(...)`? Too complex; skip colorMultiply.
    Let me build `effectsFilter(node)` returning the CSS filter string from the present effect properties.
  - OPACITY already mapped (mods.opacity).
  - CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS → ngui `[frame]` has `clipsToBounds`? No. Skip.
  - Z_INDEX → ngui `[zlayer]`? zlayer is a directive for stacking within ui-zstack. Skip or map zIndex to `[zlayer]`? Not straightforward. Skip.
  - OFFSET/POSITION → FrameOptions? No offset in FrameOptions. Skip.
  - FIXED_SIZE → no. Skip.
  - ASPECT_RATIO/CONTENT_MODE → no. Skip.
  - MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR → no. Skip.
  - LAYOUT_PRIORITY → flex has no priority. Skip.

So P3 maps:
1. Font: FONT_STYLE→font.style, LINE_SPACING→font.lineHeight.
2. Frame: MIN/MAX_WIDTH/HEIGHT → frame.minWidth/maxWidth/minHeight/maxHeight; frame.alignment when sized.
3. Shadow → mods.shadow.
4. Rotation → mods.rotation.
5. Effects filter (blur/saturation/contrast/brightness/grayscale/hueRotation/colorInvert) → mods.background.filter (or a separate `filter` on mods).
6. Underline → mods.underline (via [underline]).

// in buildMods:
const shadow = buildShadow(node);
if (shadow) mods.shadow = shadow;
const rotation = node.f32(PROPERTY.ROTATION_DEGREES);
if (rotation !== undefined && rotation !== 0) mods.rotation = rotation;
const underline = node.props().get(PROPERTY.UNDERLINE);

I've researched the current renderer structure. Here's my analysis and plan for lazy-loading the ngui components.

## Current state

`PathlandNodeComponent` (`node.component.ts` + `node.component.html`) is a single recursive component whose `imports` array eagerly pulls in **every** ngui entry point — `core`, `components` (Button/Checkbox/Toggle/RadioGroup/Menu/Option), `select`, `date-picker`, `text-area`, `text-field`, `overlay` (TriggerFor) — and one big `@switch` template. So the whole ngui surface ships in the initial bundle whether or not the app uses it.

The heavy/optional entries are the real cost: `date-picker` (calendar), `select` (combobox), `components` (menu/toggle/radio), `text-field`, `text-area`, `overlay`. The `core` entry (vstack/hstack/zstack/text/image/spacer/scroll/grid/rectangle/circle + the modifier directives) is light and effectively always needed (every tree has a root stack).

## Proposed approach: per-kind lazy nodes via `@defer`

Angular's **deferrable views** (`@defer`) are code-split into separate chunks automatically by the `@angular/build:application` builder (no router, no extra config). Each `@defer` block becomes its own chunk, fetched only when that block renders.

Structure:

1. **Keep the "core" surface eager** in `PathlandNodeComponent` (imports only `@apaq/ngui-elements/core` + the local `NotImplementedComponent`): stacks/lazy stacks, `zstack`, `grid`/lazy grids, `scrollView`, `text`, `image`, `spacer`, `color`, `shape`, the placeholder kinds (`slider/stepper/progress/gauge/colorPicker/divider/…`), and `comment`/`unknown`/`@default`. These render children via the existing `<pathland-node>` recursion.

2. **New lazy leaf nodes** under `src/app/pathland/ngui/nodes/` (each a small standalone component with a shared base for `nodeId`/`session`/mapping, importing only its own ngui entry):
   - `button-node` — `Button` (`components`)
   - `toggle-node` — `Toggle`/`Checkbox`/`Button` (`components`)
   - `text-field-node` — `TextField`/`TextFieldPrefix` (`text-field`)
   - `text-editor-node` — `TextArea` (`text-area`)
   - `picker-node` — `Select` + `Option`, `RadioGroup` + `Option`, and `Button` for segmented (`select` + `components`)
   - `menu-node` — `Button` + `Menu` + `Option` + `TriggerFor` (`components` + `overlay`)
   - `date-picker-node` — `DatePicker` (`date-picker`)

   These are all **leaves** (they render option labels from child node text, not recursive `<pathland-node>`), so there's **no import cycle** with the parent — important for reliable chunk splitting.

3. The parent template's `@case`s for these kinds become:
   ```html
   @case ('button') {
     @defer (on immediate) {
       <pathland-button-node [nodeId]="nodeId()" />
     } @placeholder { <ui-text [text]="'…'" /> }
   }
   ```
   The shared pieces (`mapping.ts`, `retained-tree`, `session.service`, the modifier directives) dedupe into a common chunk loaded once.

## Decisions to confirm

1. **Load trigger.** `@defer` needs a trigger; this also affects UX:
   - `on immediate` (recommended): chunk is still code-split and loaded only when the kind actually appears, but fetched right away — no placeholder flash, no idle/viewport wait. "Only the used components are loaded" holds because a text-only app never fetches the select/menu/date-picker chunks.
   - `on idle` / `on viewport`: true deferred timing (lazy first paint) but introduces placeholder/loading states and delayed rendering of already-mounted nodes.

2. **Scope.** (a) lazy only the control/heavy kinds listed above, keep core eager (recommended, minimal change, clean); or (b) literally every kind lazy (text/stacks/image included), maximizing chunk count but adding placeholder handling and container-recursion complexity.

3. **Picker granularity** — one `picker-node` handling all three `PICKER_STYLE`s (select/radio/segmented), or three separate nodes. I'd default to one node (it's one feature), but can split.

def case_repl(kind, tag):
    global s
    # match from the @case ('<kind>') { line through its closing "}" at the same indent
    pattern = re.compile(
        r"      @case \('" + kind + r"'\) \{\n.*?\n      \}\n",
        re.S
    )
    def sub(m):
        return ("      @case ('" + kind + "') {\n"

                "        }\n"
                "      }\n")
    s, count = pattern.subn(sub, s, count=1)
    if count != 1:

Fixed (`4833124`).

**Root cause**: ngui's `COLOR_RGBA` macro only accepts alpha as `1`, `.5`/`0.5`, or `0%` — it rejects `1.000`. `argbToRgba` was emitting three-decimal alphas (`rgba(136,136,136,1.000)`), so every color we fed into `[color]`/`[background]`/`[foregroundStyle]`/shadow was logged as "macro not supported" and ignored.

**Fix**: `argbToRgba` now trims the alpha — `1` for opaque, `0.5`/`0.502` for translucent, `0.0` for transparent — matching the ngui regex exactly. Updated the `mapping.spec` expectations to the new format.

The server-side event routing is **browser-agnostic** — both demos route identically. The only browser-visible difference the server can observe is the **`session` cookie** sent on the WebSocket handshake. Both demos derive the session id from the cookie **on every message**, falling back to a fresh `UUID.randomUUID()` when it's missing:

- Quarkus `PathlandSocket.sessionId()` (called in `@OnOpen`, `@OnBinaryMessage`, `@OnClose`).

2. `dispatch()` computes a **different** `UUID-B`, looks it up, finds nothing → the event is **silently dropped** (no update frame is emitted back).
3. `close()` similarly misses.

## Root cause
Both demos derive the session id from the `session` cookie **on every message**, falling back to a fresh `UUID.randomUUID()` when absent. With `ng serve` (no SSR visit) there's no cookie in Chrome/Firefox, so `open()` stores the `SessionApp` under one UUID while `dispatch()` computes a *different* one and finds nothing — the event is silently dropped (hence silence, no "dropping event batch" log). Safari has a leftover cookie, so it works.

## Plan

1. **Spring `PathlandSocket`**

   - Make cookie parsing **case-insensitive** (iterate `getHandshakeHeaders().entrySet()`, match `"session"` ignoring case).
2. **Quarkus `PathlandSocket`**
   - Memoize the id in a `volatile String` field at `@OnOpen` (the endpoint bean is connection-scoped); `sessionId()` returns the memoized value.

Done — committed as `a39e49d` (amended into one commit since my `git add lib/java` swept both phases together; message covers both).

## Root cause (confirmed)
Both demos derived the session id from the `session` cookie **on every message**, falling back to a fresh `UUID.randomUUID()` when absent. With `ng serve` (no SSR visit) there's no cookie in Chrome/Firefox, so `open()` stored the `SessionApp` under one UUID while `dispatch()` computed a different one and found nothing — the event was silently dropped (hence the silence). Safari had a leftover cookie, so it worked.

## Fixes
- **Spring `PathlandSocket`**: resolves the session id once at connect and memoizes it per `WebSocketSession` (`ConcurrentHashMap`); `handleMessage`/`close` reuse it; cookie lookup is now case-insensitive; binary payload copied safely (`ByteBuffer` duplicate, no `.array()`).
- **Quarkus `PathlandSocket`**: memoizes the id in a connection-scoped `volatile` field at `@OnOpen` (lazy + synchronized); case-insensitive cookie parse.
- **`DATE_CHANGED` end-to-end** (also was broken in all browsers): added `DateInput` functional interface, `PathlandNode.dateInput`, `DatePicker` wiring, an `Emitter` `dateInputs` registry exposed via `RenderResult`, and both `SessionApp.dispatch` methods now route `DATE_CHANGED` into the bound days signal (which re-emits `SET_DATE`).

## Verification
- `pathland-view` compile + **41 tests green** via the JDK-22 harness, including the new `datePickerRoutesDateIntoItsSignal`.
- Demo modules (`SessionApp`/`PathlandSocket`) are mechanical and can't be compiled locally (JDK 25 + Spring/Quarkus deps unavailable) — noted in the commit.
- Repro now: `ng serve` + backend with no SSR visit → buttons/toggles/sliders/date-picker update in Chrome/Firefox.

1: # Pathland Core Modifiers
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core modifiers** the Pathland protocol must
12: support. In the protocol these are the **`STYLE` properties**: the constraint
13: properties and visual decorations carried by `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY`. The set
14: mirrors SwiftUI's core modifiers so that any SwiftUI-shaped UI can be expressed.
15: 
16: Like SwiftUI, modifiers in Pathland are **decoupled from views**: any modifier
17: applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a `VStack` alike). A
18: modifier that a particular renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** —
19: the property is still emitted; the renderer skips it. Application code composes
20: custom modifiers from these core ones.
21: 
22: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
23: - Wire format and value types: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
24: - Events: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)
25: 
26: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
27: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
28: > defines the protocol contract only.
29: 
30: ### Emission rules
31: 
32: Each modifier emits **one or more** `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY` opcodes — one per
33: underlying property. There is no compound-modifier opcode. Compound SwiftUI
34: modifiers (`.frame(width:height:alignment:)`, `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)`,
35: `.border(_:width:)`) are expanded into several `SET_PROPERTY` opcodes, exactly
36: as the existing `.frame` modifier already does (`WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` +
37: `ALIGNMENT`).
38: 
39: `SET_PROPERTY` packing (see OPCODE.md):
40: 
41: ```
42: A = nodeId
43: B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
44: C = value (f32 bit pattern / u32 / u8 / color / arenaRef)
45: ```
46: 
47: Only **changed** properties emit: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes
48: (diff-based reactive emission). `STRING`-valued properties carry their text in
49: the frame's string section; `C` holds the arena offset.
50: 
51: ### Value types (from `value_type`, u8)
52: 
53: | Value Type | Value | `C` encoding |
54: |------------|-------|--------------|
55: | `U8` | 0x01 | low byte of C |
56: | `U32` | 0x02 | u32 |
57: | `I32` | 0x03 | i32 |
58: | `F32` | 0x04 | f32 bit pattern |
59: | `STRING` | 0x05 | arenaRef (utf8) |
60: | `ENUM` | 0x06 | low byte of C |
61: | `COLOR` | 0x07 | packed `0xAARRGGBB` (sRGB) |
62: | `DESIGN_TOKEN` | 0x08 | arenaRef (token path) |
63: 
64: Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1.0` = `FILL` (expand to available), `-2.0` =
65: `HUG_CONTENT` (native intrinsic size).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 1. Layout
70: 
71: Arrangement and sizing. These map to the native renderer's layout knobs.
72: 
73: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
74: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
75: | `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` | `WIDTH` 0x100B, `HEIGHT` 0x100C, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002 | F32, F32, ENUM | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided axis/alignment |
76: | `.frame(minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:minHeight:idealHeight:maxHeight:)` | `MIN_WIDTH` 0x0012, `IDEAL_WIDTH` 0x0013, `MAX_WIDTH` 0x0014, `MIN_HEIGHT` 0x0015, `IDEAL_HEIGHT` 0x0016, `MAX_HEIGHT` 0x0017 | F32 | one `SET_PROPERTY` per provided bound |
77: | `.padding(_:)`, `.padding(edges:)`, `.padding(_:edges:)` | `PADDING` 0x1011, `PADDING_TOP` 0x1012, `PADDING_RIGHT` 0x1013, `PADDING_BOTTOM` 0x1014, `PADDING_LEFT` 0x1015 | F32 | uniform → one; per-edge → per-edge |
78: | `.offset(x:y:)` | `OFFSET_X` 0x000E, `OFFSET_Y` 0x000F | F32 | two |
79: | `.position(x:y:)` | `POSITION_X` 0x0010, `POSITION_Y` 0x0011 | F32 | two |
80: | `.fixedSize()` / `.fixedSize(horizontal:vertical:)` | `FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL` 0x0018, `FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL` 0x0019 | U8 (0/1) | two (or one when axis-limited) |
81: | `.layoutPriority(_:)` | `LAYOUT_PRIORITY` 0x001A | F32 | one |
82: | `.zIndex(_:)` | `Z_INDEX` 0x100F | F32 | one |
83: | `.aspectRatio(_:contentMode:)` | `ASPECT_RATIO` 0x001B, `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | F32, ENUM | two |
84: | `.scaledToFit()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fit`=0) | one |
85: | `.scaledToFill()` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C | ENUM (`Fill`=1) | one |
86: | `.minimumScaleFactor(_:)` | `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR` 0x001D | F32 | one |
87: | `.spacing(_:)` (stacks) | `SPACING` 0x0001 | F32 | one |
88: | `Spacer` | — (implied by component) | — | none |
89: 
90: ### Semantics
91: 
92: - **`WIDTH` / `HEIGHT`**: size hints; the renderer maps them to its size
93:   request / `width`/`height` style. `FILL` (-1.0) expands to available space;
94:   `HUG_CONTENT` (-2.0) sizes to intrinsic content. Absence of a property leaves
95:   that axis to the native default.
96: - **`frame(min/ideal/max)`**: each provided bound emits its own property.
97:   Renderers map them to min/max/ideal size (GTK `set_size_request`, CSS
98:   `min-width`/`max-width`/`width`).
99: - **`PADDING` vs per-edge**: `PADDING` is uniform and shorthand; a per-edge
100:   modifier overwrites the edge only. Per-edge wins over uniform when both are
101:   present.
102: - **`ALIGNMENT` enum**: `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3.
103: - **`CONTENT_MODE` enum**: `Fit`=0 (aspect-fit within the bounds),
104:   `Fill`=1 (aspect-fill, cropped).
105: - **`OFFSET`** moves the element **after** layout without affecting layout
106:   (post-layout translation; GTK margins/translation, CSS `transform:
107:   translate`).
108: - **`POSITION`** is absolute placement within the parent (CSS `position:
109:   absolute; left/top`); the renderer resolves the anchor.
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## 2. Text Formatting
114: 
115: Apply to `Text`, `Label`, `Button` labels, and text-bearing controls. Renderers
116: map them to their native text attributes.
117: 
118: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
119: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
120: | `.font(.system(size:))` | `FONT_SIZE` 0x1007 | F32 | one |
121: | `.fontWeight(_:)` | `FONT_WEIGHT` 0x1008 | F32 (100–900) | one |
122: | `.font(.custom(name:size:))` | `FONT_FAMILY` 0x1009 | STRING | one (arenaRef) |
123: | `.italic()` / `.fontStyle(_:)` | `FONT_STYLE` 0x1017 | ENUM (`Normal`=0, `Italic`=1) | one |
124: | `.fontDesign(_:)` | `FONT_DESIGN` 0x1018 | ENUM (`Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3) | one |
125: | `.fontWidth(_:)` | `FONT_WIDTH` 0x1019 | F32 (0.5–1.5, 1.0 default) | one |
126: | `.kerning(_:)` | `KERNING` 0x101A | F32 | one |
127: | `.tracking(_:)` | `TRACKING` 0x101B | F32 | one |
128: | `.baselineOffset(_:)` | `BASELINE_OFFSET` 0x101C | F32 | one |
129: | `.lineSpacing(_:)` | `LINE_SPACING` 0x101D | F32 | one |
130: | `.lineLimit(_:)` | `LINE_LIMIT` 0x000B | U32 | one |
131: | `.multilineTextAlignment(_:)` | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` 0x000C | ENUM (`Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2) | one |
132: | `.truncationMode(_:)` | `TRUNCATION_MODE` 0x000D | ENUM (`Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2) | one |
133: | `.textCase(_:)` | `TEXT_CASE` 0x101E | ENUM (`None`=0, `Uppercase`=1, `Lowercase`=2) | one |
134: | `.underline()` | `UNDERLINE` 0x101F | U8 (0/1) | one |
135: | `.strikethrough()` | `STRIKETHROUGH` 0x1020 | U8 (0/1) | one |
136: | `.foregroundStyle(_:)` | `COLOR` 0x100A | COLOR | one |
137: | `.tint(_:)` | `TINT` 0x1030 | COLOR | one |
138: 
139: > **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` exists only as a **View** (a
140: > layout-greedy solid-color fill) and as a **Data Type** passed into
141: > style-taking modifiers (`.foregroundStyle(_:)`, `.background(_:)`,
142: > `.border(_:)`, `.tint(_:)`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier and
143: > `.foregroundColor(_:)` is deprecated — all foreground styling uses
144: > `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
145: 
146: \* `FONT_FAMILY` is a `STRING` property (arenaRef), matching SwiftUI, which
147: passes font families as string names (`.font(.custom("Georgia", size:))`).
148: 
149: ### Semantics
150: 
151: - **`FONT_WEIGHT`** is a numeric F32 on the 100–900 scale (`regular`≈400,
152:   `bold`≈700). Renderers map it to the nearest native weight.
153: - **`KERNING` vs `TRACKING`**: kerning adjusts per-glyph spacing at a
154:   point/em scale; tracking adds uniform letter spacing. Both are F32 points.
155: - **`LINE_LIMIT`** of 0 means unlimited.
156: - **`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`** differs from stack `ALIGNMENT`: it aligns the text block
157:   inside its own bounds (CSS `text-align`), not children of a stack.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 3. Appearance & Effects
162: 
163: Visual decoration. These never change layout; they decorate the element.
164: 
165: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
166: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
167: | `.background(_:)` | `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001 | COLOR | one |
168: | `.border(_:width:)` | `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `BORDER_WIDTH` 0x1003 | COLOR, F32 | two |
169: | `.border(_:width:edges:)` | `BORDER_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`, `BORDER_EDGES` 0x1016 | COLOR, F32, U32 (bitmask) | three |
170: | `.cornerRadius(_:)` | `BORDER_RADIUS` 0x1005 | F32 | one |
171: | `.shadow(color:radius:x:y:)` | `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `SHADOW_RADIUS` 0x1022, `SHADOW_X` 0x1023, `SHADOW_Y` 0x1024 | COLOR, F32, F32, F32 | four |
172: | `.opacity(_:)` | `OPACITY` 0x100D | F32 (0–1) | one |
173: | `.blur(radius:)` | `BLUR_RADIUS` 0x1025 | F32 | one |
174: | `.saturation(_:)` | `SATURATION` 0x1026 | F32 (0–1) | one |
175: | `.contrast(_:)` | `CONTRAST` 0x1027 | F32 (0–1) | one |
176: | `.brightness(_:)` | `BRIGHTNESS` 0x1028 | F32 (−1–1) | one |
177: | `.grayscale(_:)` | `GRAYSCALE` 0x1029 | F32 (0–1) | one |
178: | `.hueRotation(_:)` | `HUE_ROTATION` 0x102A | F32 (degrees) | one |
179: | `.colorMultiply(_:)` | `COLOR_MULTIPLY` 0x102B | COLOR | one |
180: | `.colorInvert()` | `COLOR_INVERT` 0x102C | U8 (0/1) | one |
181: | `.clipped()` / `.clipsToBounds` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 | U8 (0/1) | one |
182: | `.clipShape(_:)` | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` 0x1010 + `SHAPE_KIND` 0x0006 | U8 + ENUM | two (see note) |
183: 
184: ### Semantics
185: 
186: - **`BORDER_EDGES`** is a u32 bitmask: `TOP`=1, `LEADING`=2, `BOTTOM`=4,
187:   `TRAILING`=8 (direction-aware; see OPCODE.md). When `.border` has no `edges:`
188:   argument the renderer treats the mask as `ALL` (0xF).
189: - **`BORDER_RADIUS`** rounds all corners; a future per-corner variant would add
190:   `TOP_LEFT_*`/… properties.
191: - **`SHADOW`** is a compound: exactly four `SET_PROPERTY` opcodes. Missing
192:   fields default: color = token `color.shadow`, radius = 0, x = 0, y = 0.
193: - **`clipShape`**: `SHAPE_KIND` (0x0006, defined in
194:   [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md#5-shapes--paints)) selects the clip geometry;
195:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` (1) turns clipping on. A bare `.clipped()` is
196:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` with no shape.
197: - **Color effects** (`SATURATION`, `CONTRAST`, …) are renderer-owned filters;
198:   the renderer maps them to native filter APIs (CSS `filter`, GTK
199:   `GtkSnapshot` effects). They compose in the order applied.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 4. Transform
204: 
205: Geometric transforms applied after layout.
206: 
207: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property(ies) | Type | Emission |
208: | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------ | ---------- |
209: | `.rotationEffect(_:anchor:)` | `ROTATION_DEGREES` 0x102D | F32 (degrees, counter-clockwise) | one (anchor is renderer-token-owned) |
210: | `.scaleEffect(_:anchor:)` | `SCALE` 0x102E | F32 (uniform scale) | one (anchor is renderer-token-owned) |
211: 
212: ### Semantics
213: 
214: - Transforms do **not** affect layout; the renderer applies them as a
215:   post-layout visual transform (CSS `transform`, GTK `gtk_widget_allocate`
216:   transform).
217: - **Anchor** is renderer-token-owned (`.center` default); the protocol does not
218:   transmit anchors — the renderer owns presentation (see OPCODE.md design
219:   tokens). Non-uniform scale / 3D rotation are future extensions.
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## 5. Interaction & State
224: 
225: Semantic properties controlling whether and how an element responds to input,
226: plus accessibility. These are the "semantic" (`0x2000`) properties.
227: 
228: | SwiftUI modifier | Protocol property | Type | Emission |
229: | ------------------ | ------------------- | ------ | ---------- |
230: | `.hidden()` | `VISIBLE` 0x100E | U8 (0 = hidden) | one |
231: | `.disabled(_:)` | `ENABLED` 0x2003 | U8 (1 = enabled) | one |
232: | `.allowsHitTesting(_:)` | `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING` 0x102F | U8 (0/1) | one |
233: | `.controlSize(_:)` | `CONTROL_SIZE` 0x200C | ENUM (`Small`=0, `Regular`=1, `Large`=2) | one |
234: | `.focusable(_:)` | — (via `FOCUS` listener) | — | none (declares `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit 5) |
235: | `.accessibilityLabel(_:)` | `LABEL` 0x200A | STRING | one (arenaRef) |
236: | `.accessibilityRole(_:)` | `ROLE` 0x2001 | ENUM | one |
237: | `.accessibilityState(_:)` | `STATE` 0x2002 | ENUM | one |
238: 
239: ### Semantics
240: 
241: - **`VISIBLE`**: 0 hides the element entirely (removed from layout and hit
242:   testing by the renderer); 1 shows it. Diff-based emission means toggling
243:   visibility emits a single `SET_PROPERTY`.
244: - **`ENABLED`** is the inverse of SwiftUI `.disabled()`: 1 = interactive, 0 =
245:   disabled. Disabled controls do not emit events.
246: - **`.focusable`** has no property: the app requests focus events via the
247:   `FOCUS` listener bit (`EVENT_LISTENERS`, bit 5) and observes
248:   `EVENT::FOCUS_CHANGED` — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md).
249: - **`ROLE`/`STATE`** are accessibility enums; their enumerated values are
250:   defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#semantic-properties), not here. `STATE` is
251:   a semantic accessibility property — it never describes visual styling.
252: - **`LABEL`** is a `STRING` property (the accessibility label), distinct from a
253:   `TEXT_FIELD`'s caption label.
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## Property ID Catalog
258: 
259: ### Allocated property IDs
260: 
261: | Range | Group |
262: | ------- | ------- |
263: | `0x0001`–`0x0005` | Stack constraint (SPACING, ALIGNMENT, …, CONTENT_MARGINS) |
264: | `0x0006` | `SHAPE_KIND` (ENUM; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
265: | `0x000A`–`0x000D` | Text (TEXT, LINE_LIMIT, TEXT_ALIGNMENT, TRUNCATION_MODE) |
266: | `0x000E`–`0x001D` | Layout properties (allocated: OFFSET, POSITION, frame bounds, FIXED_SIZE, LAYOUT_PRIORITY, ASPECT_RATIO/CONTENT_MODE, MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR) |
267: | `0x001E`–`0x00FF` | Future layout/format properties (unallocated) |
268: | `0x1001`–`0x1016` | Styling (BACKGROUND_COLOR, BORDER_*, FONT_SIZE/WEIGHT/FAMILY, COLOR, WIDTH, HEIGHT, OPACITY, VISIBLE, Z_INDEX, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS, PADDING_*, BORDER_EDGES) |
269: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (STRING; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
270: | `0x1017`–`0x102F` | Text-format properties (allocated: FONT_STYLE/DESIGN/WIDTH, KERNING, TRACKING, BASELINE_OFFSET, LINE_SPACING, TEXT_CASE, UNDERLINE, STRIKETHROUGH), effect properties (SHADOW_*, BLUR, SATURATION, CONTRAST, BRIGHTNESS, GRAYSCALE, HUE_ROTATION, COLOR_MULTIPLY, COLOR_INVERT), ROTATION_DEGREES, SCALE, ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING |
271: | `0x1030` | `TINT` (COLOR) | — |
272: | `0x1030`–`0x10FF` | Future styling properties (unallocated) |
273: | `0x2001`–`0x200B` | Semantic (ROLE, STATE, ENABLED, SELECTED, EVENT_LISTENERS, VALUE, MIN_VALUE, MAX_VALUE, LABEL, PROMPT) |
274: | `0x2009`, `0x200C`–`0x2014` | Control properties (allocated: STEP_VALUE, CONTROL_SIZE, IS_SECURE, PROGRESS, IS_INDETERMINATE, SELECTION, COLOR_VALUE, DATE_PICKER_MODE, PICKER_STYLE) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md controls. Note: a `DATE_PICKER`'s date is set via the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (0x04), not a property; **`0x2011` is unallocated/reserved** (its former `DATE_VALUE` draft was dropped) |
275: | `0x2016`–`0x2018` | Binding/action properties (allocated: `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md semantic controls |
276: | `0x2015`, `0x2019`–`0x20FF` | Future semantic properties (unallocated) |
277: 
278: ### Reserved ranges
279: 
280: | Range | Use |
281: |-------|-----|
282: | `0x0003`, `0x0004` | Reserved (formerly JUSTIFICATION, PADDING) — MUST NOT be reused |
283: | `0x0007`–`0x0009`, `0x000E`+ high | Draft/future layout |
284: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (allocated) |
285: 
286: A renderer MUST ignore unknown property ids and continue decoding.
287: 
288: ### Default value type resolution
289: 
290: The canonical value type per property (the protocol's authoritative mapping):
291: 
292: - `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_COLOR`, `COLOR_MULTIPLY`,
293:   `SHADOW_COLOR`, `COLOR_VALUE`, `TINT` → `COLOR`
294: - `EVENT_LISTENERS`, `BORDER_EDGES` → `U32`
295: - `SELECTED`, `VISIBLE`, `ENABLED`, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`,
296:   `COLOR_INVERT`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `IS_SECURE`,
297:   `IS_INDETERMINATE`, `FIXED_SIZE_*` → `U8`
298: - `LABEL`, `PROMPT`, `FONT_FAMILY`, `IMAGE_SOURCE` → `STRING`
299: - `LINE_LIMIT`, `SELECTION`, `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID` → `U32`
300: - `ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`,
301:   `FONT_DESIGN`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `SHAPE_KIND`,
302:   `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, `PICKER_STYLE`, `TOGGLE_STYLE` → `F32` (numeric enum code;
303:   see the appendix and [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#value-types))
304: - everything else → `F32`
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## Appendix: Enumerated values
309: 
310: Single authoritative source for every enum-valued property in the protocol.
311: A renderer or emitter MUST use these exact numeric codes. The code is carried
312: in the property value as an **f32 bit pattern** (`value_type::F32`) — see the
313: [value-type
314: conventions](./OPCODE.md#value-types) and the [default value type
315: resolution](#default-value-type-resolution).
316: 
317: | Property | ID | Values |
318: |----------|----|--------|
319: | `ALIGNMENT` | 0x0002 | `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3 |
320: | `SHAPE_KIND` | 0x0006 | `Circle`=0, `Rectangle`=1, `RoundedRectangle`=2, `Capsule`=3, `Ellipse`=4, `Path`=5 |
321: | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` | 0x000C | `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2 |
322: | `TRUNCATION_MODE` | 0x000D | `Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2 |
323: | `CONTENT_MODE` | 0x001C | `Fit`=0, `Fill`=1 |
324: | `FONT_STYLE` | 0x1017 | `Normal`=0, `Italic`=1 |
325: | `FONT_DESIGN` | 0x1018 | `Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3 |
326: | `TEXT_CASE` | 0x101E | `None`=0, `Uppercase`=1, `Lowercase`=2 |
327: | `CONTROL_SIZE` | 0x200C | `Small`=0, `Regular`=1, `Large`=2 |
328: | `DATE_PICKER_MODE` | 0x2013 | `Date`=0, `Time`=1, `DateAndTime`=2 |
329: | `PICKER_STYLE` | 0x2014 | `Menu`=0, `Segmented`=1, `Wheel`=2, `RadioGroup`=3 |
330: | `TOGGLE_STYLE` | 0x2018 | `Switch`=0 (default), `Checkbox`=1, `Button`=2 |
331: 
332: Non-`ENUM` scales:
333: 
334: - `FONT_WEIGHT` (0x1008) is a numeric F32 on the 100–900 scale
335:   (`regular`≈400, `bold`≈700), not an enum.
336: - `ROLE` (0x2001) and `STATE` (0x2002) are accessibility enums; their value
337:   sets are defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#semantic-properties) and are not
338:   reproduced here.
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## Conformance
343: 
344: New properties added here MUST be reflected in `pathland-core`'s diff emitter
345: and the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) before renderers
346: depend on them.

3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,

11: //! free `text`/`spacer` functions, then chain modifiers and `build()`:
12: //!
13: //! ```
14: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, hstack, text, View, ViewExt};
15: //!
16: //! let node = vstack![
17: //!     text("a"),

23: //! ```

26: //!

28: //! to any view via the blanket `View::modifier`, and application code composes
29: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:

34: //! struct Card;
35: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
36: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
37: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
38: //!         Background(Color(0xFF_EEEEEE)).apply(node);
39: //!     }
40: //! }
41: //!
42: //! // Works on any view:
43: //! let a = pathland_view::text("A").modifier(Card);
44: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].modifier(Card);
45: //! # let _ = (a, b);
46: //! ```
47: //!
48: //! Unsupported combinations are **allowed and ignored**: the modifier emits its
49: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.
50: //!
51: //! ## No layout math
52: //!
53: //! The DSL describes structure + constraint properties only. It never computes
54: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.
55: //!
56: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`.

92: /// Build a vertical stack from a comma-separated list of views.
93: ///
94: /// Each child is boxed automatically, so children can mix `Text`, `HStack`,
95: /// modified views, or custom `View` implementations. Nested stacks work:
96: ///
97: /// ```
98: /// use pathland_view::{vstack, text, View};
99: /// let node = vstack![text("a"), text("b")].build();
100: /// # let _ = node;
101: /// ```
102: #[macro_export]
103: macro_rules! vstack {
104:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
105:         $crate::VStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
106:     };
107: }
108: 
109: /// Build a horizontal stack from a comma-separated list of views.
110: ///
111: /// See [`vstack!`] for details.
112: #[macro_export]
113: macro_rules! hstack {
114:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
115:         $crate::HStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
116:     };
117: }

129: /// Cross-axis alignment values for stacks and the `Frame` compound modifier.
130: ///
131: /// These are emitted as the `ALIGNMENT` (0x0002) property with an `ENUM` value
132: /// type (low byte of the property value).
133: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
134: pub enum Align {
135:     /// Align to the leading (start) edge.
136:     Leading,
137:     /// Center along the cross axis.
138:     Center,
139:     /// Align to the trailing (end) edge.
140:     Trailing,
141:     /// Fill the available cross-axis space.
142:     Fill,
143: }
144: 
145: impl Align {
146:     /// The protocol enum value for this alignment.
147:     pub fn value(self) -> u8 {
148:         match self {
149:             Align::Leading => 0,
150:             Align::Center => 1,
151:             Align::Trailing => 2,
152:             Align::Fill => 3,
153:         }
154:     }
155: }
