I have a good picture of the design-system landscape. The candidates cluster around **CSS-custom-property token systems that are themeable/overridable**. Let me synthesize which makes the most sense for Pathland's specific constraints: pure Rust-emitted HTML with inline `<style>`, a **static safelist already gone**, design tokens over the protocol adjusting the design via CSS variables.

## Design-system analysis for Pathland

Pathland's constraint is unusual: we emit HTML with **inline `<style>` tags**, no build step, and want **design tokens over the protocol** (via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) to adjust the design. This points to a **pure-CSS, custom-property-based** token system — not one tied to Tailwind v4 `@theme` (since we're dropping Tailwind).

The candidates and fit:

| System | Token approach | Tailwind dependency | Pathland fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Inkwell** | Pure-CSS `:root` custom properties, `light-dark()`, ~30 component classes, no build | Optional (has a v4 entry) | **Best pure-CSS fit** — no build, token overrides via `:root`, component classes, dark mode |
| **Response UI CSS** | CSS custom properties, responsive tokens, overrideable theme contract | Intended for Tailwind v4 | Decent, but assumes Tailwind for layout |
| **Mastors** | SCSS token maps → custom properties | SCSS build (not pure CSS) | Requires SCSS build — conflicts with pure inline |
| **System One / democrito / Clay** | CSS custom properties, but React/Tailwind-oriented | Heavy React/Tailwind | Not a fit (framework-bound) |

**My recommendation: don't adopt a third-party design system wholesale.** Instead, **adopt the pattern**: a small, self-contained **custom-property token layer** we author ourselves in the renderer's `<style>` block (like Inkwell's token-first approach), because:
1. Pathland's renderer emits **pure HTML + inline `<style>`** — a vendored third-party CSS system (especially Tailwind-coupled ones) fights this.
2. We control the exact tokens, and **`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` over the protocol maps directly to `:root` custom properties** (`--pl-accent`, `--pl-surface`, `--pl-radius`, …) — this is the clean, native way to let protocol design tokens adjust the design.
3. **Inkwell** is the closest off-the-shelf match and MIT-licensed — we could **vendor its token-layer approach** (or even its tokens) as our starting baseline, then adapt.

So the plan: **define our own tokenized design-system baseline** (a `:root` custom-property block + component `.pathland-*` rules), inspired by Inkwell's pure-CSS token architecture, with `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overriding those custom properties. This gives us Tailwind's *layout* philosophy (via inline styles, which the renderer already does) + overrideable style variables + a coherent default look.

## Full plan — revert to inline-all + our own CSS design system

### 1. Rust renderer (`pathland-render-html`)

**a. Inline-all emission (`style_css`):**
- Move **every** property to inline `style`, including the currently-enum ones:
  - `ALIGNMENT` → `align-items:flex-start|center|flex-end|stretch`
  - `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` → `text-align:left|center|right`
  - `TEXT_CASE` → `text-transform:uppercase|lowercase`
  - `VISIBLE=0` → `display:none`
  - stack direction → `display:flex;flex-direction:column|row`
  - `w-full`/`w-fit` → `width:100%`/`width:fit-content`
  - `hidden` → `display:none`
  - grid `grid-cols-N` → `display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(N,1fr)`
- All arbitrary-number (dp) already inline. So **every opcode property** → inline.

**b. Built-in `<style>` block (our own CSS):**
- Include **Tailwind's reset** (preflight) as our own base (vendored, license MIT) — `box-sizing`, margins, etc.
- Define a **`<style>` block with `:root` custom properties** (our design tokens): `--pl-accent`, `--pl-surface`, `--pl-text`, `--pl-border`, `--pl-muted`, `--pl-radius`, `--pl-focus-ring`, spacing scale, etc.
- **Component `.pathland-*` classes** for the default look (toggle switch knob/animation, spinner, gauge, button, inputs, slider, menu), written against the tokens.
- **Button prettify (our POC)**: `.pathland-button` (or `button {}`) with the rounded/bg/shadow/inset-ring/hover/focus-visible/disabled look from the example — as plain CSS using tokens.

**c. Delete Tailwind:**
- Remove `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs` (or reduce to the reset/token CSS), `pathland_tailwind_compile` C ABI, the `tailwind-embed` feature + `build.rs` embed, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`, `vendor/`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` Tailwind section.
- `render_document` drops the `/tailwind.css` link; the `<style>` block is inline.

### 2. Design tokens over the protocol
- `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (already wired in the DOM renderer + token sink) sets `:root` custom properties. Align our `:root` token names with the protocol's token paths (`color.accent`, `color.surface`, `space.2`, `font.body`, `radius.md`, …) so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN("color.accent", ...)` rethemes the renderer's `<style>` block. This is the cleanest linkage.

### 3. Java shim + demos
- Remove `compileTailwind`; delete `TailwindCssController`/`TailwindCssResource`; `SessionApp.renderHtml` no longer links `/tailwind.css`.

### 4. CI / packaging
- Remove Tailwind fetch/vendor-cache/artifact steps; Rust job builds the plain renderer; jar embeds only the renderer dylib (much smaller, no Tailwind binary).

### 5. TS DOM renderer
- Already all-inline — **no change** (aligns perfectly). 

### 6. Tests
- Update Rust tests: all properties assert inline; remove Tailwind-compile tests; add a test asserting the `<style>` block contains the reset + `:root` tokens + `.pathland-button`.
- Update Java/demo tests (remove tailwind references).

## Questions before I finalize

1. **Design-system source**: vendor **Inkwell's token architecture** (MIT, pure-CSS custom properties) as our baseline and adapt, or **author our own token layer** from scratch (inspired by Inkwell)? I lean **author our own** (smaller, exactly tailored, no third-party surface), unless you want Inkwell's ready-made components.
2. **Button POC target**: implement the button exactly like your example (rounded, bg-white, shadow, inset-ring, hover:bg-gray-50, plus `dark:` via `prefers-color-scheme`) — as plain CSS in the block. Confirm the dark-mode handling (media-query `prefers-color-scheme` vs a `.dark`/`[data-theme]` attribute we toggle).
3. **Token→protocol linkage**: confirm we map `:root` custom properties to protocol token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme (my proposed design). 
4. **Reset**: vendor Tailwind's preflight (MIT) verbatim as our base reset, or a leaner custom reset? (You said "include the reset that tailwind uses" — so verbatim preflight, confirmed.)
5. **Delete vs keep-dormant** Tailwind code — you said delete; confirm the full removal (binary feature, fetch script, compile, `/tailwind.css`, CI tailwind steps).

Once you confirm, I'll produce the precise file-by-file implementation plan.
1: author our own 2: Yes, but create the design tokens needed for it. 3: yes 4: What are pros and cons? 5: full removal.

Decisions noted. Let me quickly verify the Tailwind preflight (reset) specifics so I can give you a concrete pros/cons on #4 (read-only).

The Tailwind "preflight" reset is their base stylesheet built on top of **modern-normalize** (or pre-modern-normalize, their own). It includes:
- `*, ::before, ::after { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0 }` (border-box on everything)
- `html { line-height: 1.5; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% }`
- Removes default list styles, `a { color: inherit; text-decoration: inherit }`, `button/input/select/textarea` font/color inheritance, image `display:block; max-width:100%`, form control reset, etc.
- It's MIT-licensed (Tailwind is MIT, preflight ships with it).

Let me lay out the pros/cons for the reset question, then the full plan.

## Question 4 — pros/cons: vendor Tailwind preflight verbatim vs a leaner custom reset

**Option A — vendor Tailwind's preflight verbatim (MIT)**
- Pros: battle-tested, comprehensive, matches what everyone expects (box-sizing border-box, sensible defaults); it's exactly "the reset Tailwind uses," which you asked to include; low maintenance (copy once); guaranteed consistent behavior across browsers/elements.
- Cons: it's larger than needed and opinionated in places we may not want (e.g. it strips some default semantics, makes `img` `display:block` which could surprise, resets form controls aggressively). Some of its choices assume a Tailwind-utility authoring model. We'd be importing rules we don't all use.
- Licensing: MIT, fine to vendor with attribution.

**Option B — leaner custom reset (we author)**
- Pros: exactly our needs; smaller; we control every rule; can align closely with the `.pathland-*` design tokens; no "foreign" opinionated rules.
- Cons: we re-derive what preflight already solved; risk of missing edge-case resets (form controls, media, etc.); more effort to get "battle-tested" parity.

**My recommendation:** Since you explicitly said "include the reset that Tailwind uses," and to honor that precisely, I'd **vendor Tailwind's preflight verbatim** (Option A) as our base reset — it's MIT, comprehensive, and exactly what you asked for — and then layer our own `.pathland-*`/token CSS on top. A leaner custom reset can be a later refinement if the size/behavior bothers us.

Now, the full plan with all your decisions:

## Full plan — revert to inline-all styling + our own tokenized design system

### Confirmed decisions
1. **Author our own** design-system/token layer (not third-party).
2. **Button POC** in plain CSS using our own design tokens.
3. **`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` → `:root` custom properties** (protocol tokens retheme the renderer).
4. **Vendor Tailwind preflight verbatim** as our base reset (MIT).

## Objective
- Turn Pathland into a grant-ready, production-ready open standard. The user (solo dev, **Apaq ApS**) is preparing an NLnet / "Open Internet Stack" proposal (reopens **Sept 3 2026**, deadline **Nov 3 2026 noon CET**) for a small first grant (~€11,700), but has deprioritized the grant timeline in favor of **full-speed product development** to make Pathland a credible **enterprise-SRE replacement for HTMX and the whole BFF + Rich Frontend paradigm**.
- The enterprise-SRE foundation (P0–P2a + P2b + fixes) has been merged to `main`. The current active work is **reverting the HTML renderer to pure inline styling** (drop Tailwind) and **building our own tokenized design system** with a prettified button.

## Important Details
- **Grant decisions (locked):** core-first scope, demo-as-evidence, applicant **Apaq ApS** (VAT **DK41717955**, **apaq.dk**, **Michael Krog mic@apaq.dk**), **€45/h** cost-recovery, **260 h**, total **€11,700**, project **Jan–Jun 2027**. Goal = "foot in the door"; money is secondary to being accepted as a quality assessment. Grant doc re-scope is deferred until after the product push (user: "After").
- **Strategic pivot (user-confirmed):** do not wait for the grant (approval ~Dec 2026); work at full speed on making Pathland an HTMX/BFF-SPA replacement for enterprise SRE. Grant must fund "things that can be improved after" that work.
- **Java 17 whole-stack (locked):** replace `ScopedValue`→thread-local, `FFM`→`JNA`, `maven.compiler.release=17`, CI Temurin 17/21/25 matrix.
- **DOM renderer (locked):** `@pathland/dom-renderer` (TS, `lib/typescript/`), single source replacing the duplicated `app.js`; full spec-catalog conformance (all modifiers/control variants/events/`EVENT_LISTENERS` gating); `META::RESYNC` protocol-first (no-replay-on-connect; server sends full snapshot only on explicit request); hydration-aware TREE reconciliation; resync-on-reconnect.
- **Renderer architecture (locked):** stateless streaming Rust `pathland-render-html` (one-pass over a snapshot batch, transient decode map, no retained tree); C ABI `pathland_html_render`/`_render_fragment`/`_free`; Java JNA shim (`com.pathland.render.html`).
- **Tailwind decisions (now being reverted):** after building the Tailwind v4 pipeline (embedded per-platform standalone binary, `tailwind-embed` feature, `pathland_tailwind_compile`, `compileTailwind`), the user decided **Tailwind has "too many quirks" and to revert to inline styling for ALL opcodes** (decision A). Include Tailwind's preflight reset as our own CSS, delivered inline in `<style>` tags. **Full removal** of all Tailwind machinery. **Ship Inter** as the default font. **Author our own** design-token layer (not third-party). **Button prettify** is the POC. Design tokens align to protocol token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme.
- **Spacing semantics (locked earlier):** arbitrary-number (dp/point) styling renders inline as CSS px (1 dp = 1 CSS px); only finite protocol-enum values were Tailwind classes — now even those are inline.
- **Verification:** Java compiles/tests via JDK-17 (`/Users/michael/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/corretto-17.0.16/Contents/Home`) and JDK-21; Quarkus/Spring demos compile locally on JDK 17 (deps cached), CI-only otherwise.

## Work State
### Completed
- **P0–P2a + P2b + fixes merged to `main`** via PR #75 (`fa8605b`): Java 17 whole-stack; TS DOM renderer + full-catalog conformance; no-replay-on-connect + `META::RESYNC`; stateless streaming Rust renderer + C ABI; Tailwind emission (Phases 1+2); Tailwind v4 integration (feature-gated embedded binary); Java JNA shim; Cargo collision fix.
- **Java-embedding of the Rust dylib** (`9632ab0`): jar embeds `libpathland_render_html` at `META-INF/native/`, extracted via JNA; graceful degradation (`tryInstance`/`isAvailable`); fail-loud jar-embed pom step.
- **CI fixed** (PR #75 checks green): Java job `needs: [rust]` + artifact handoff; Rust job fetches real Tailwind standalone binary (cached), builds `--features tailwind-embed`, uploads artifact; fixed Rust-target-triple vendor dir (`TARGET_TO_ASSET` map); platform-aware embedded-library test. Issue #76 filed (compile demos in CI).
- **Tailwind real-binary integration** (`6643bcb`): real `tailwindcss v4.3.3` standalone (MIT) embedded; `/tailwind.css` returns real compiled CSS from the Spring fat jar with no `java.library.path`. Issue #77 closed. Robustness fixes in `compile()`/`extract_embedded()`.
- **Inline-arbitrary + finite static safelist** (PR #78, `4fe3b1f` merged to main): dropped the `classes` param from `pathland_tailwind_compile`/`compileTailwind`; `tw::safelist()` became finite static set; arbitrary dp → inline.
- **Current branch `feature/inline-css-design-system`** (off `main`): inline-all emission partially done.
- Earlier work (from prior summary) still valid: DSL convergence, spec/DSL.md, governance trio, GRANT.md rewrite (since superseded by pivot), grant backlog issues #37–#50.

### Active
- **Reverting to inline-all styling + own design system** (branch `feature/inline-css-design-system`, current work):
  - `lib.rs`: added enum-derived properties inline to `style_css()` (ALIGNMENT, TEXT_ALIGNMENT, TEXT_CASE, VISIBLE, FONT_STYLE, FONT_DESIGN, UNDERLINE/STRIKETHROUGH, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS, ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING, COLOR_INVERT, TRUNCATION); added `style_attr()` method; removed `style_classes()` and `decor()`; removed `mod tw;` and `mod tailwind;`; updated `render_node` (removed `classes`/`class` plumbing); rewrote grid/scrollview/zstack cases to inline styles; rewrote `wrap_stack` to inline flex + alignment; added `grid_style()` fn; renamed module decl to `mod css;`.

# pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 1, 2026

The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming**
pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call
decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once,
and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer
Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)`
  / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML;
  the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed.
- **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy:
  `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`, `VSTACK`/
  `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/
  `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD`
  (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE`
  (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
  `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children + `SELECTION`), `MENU`,
  `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`.
- **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render
  the custom body wrapped in the native element.
- **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis flex), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
  `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL`/`HUG`), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
  `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
  `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`,
  `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA), plus
  `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`,
  `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `COLOR_INVERT`.
- **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` /
  `data-binding-id` attributes.
- `STYLE::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time).

## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system

Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a
single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist:

- **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`),
  including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment,
  text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds,
  hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**.
- **`css::STYLE`** is a built-in `<style>` block injected by `render_document`,
  containing:
  - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see
    `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`),
  - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-accent`,
    `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, button tokens),
    named to match the protocol design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can
    retheme the renderer,
  - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme`
    dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text
    field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/
    disabled states that can't be expressed inline.
- **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` /
  `_free`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA shim). The `_tailwind_compile`
  entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`,
  `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**.

## Not implemented / gaps

- `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property).
- GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact.
- The Inter webfont is referenced by `--pl-font-sans` but **not yet bundled**;
  the CSS falls back to `system-ui` until the OFL-licensed woff2 is embedded
  (documented follow-up — see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`).

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 27 headless render tests (components,
properties, composite, event attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames,
inline-all styling, built-in CSS block contents).

input.newString:
## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Full Rust renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, and literal colors inline. The renderer injects its own
  built-in `<style>` block (preflight reset + design tokens + `.pathland-*`
  component defaults) into every document — no external CSS, no `/tailwind.css`.
- **Demos use the shim**: `SessionApp` no longer calls `applyFrame`; SSR renders
  the mount frame through `HtmlRenderer.render(sink.frame(), rootId)`. The
  renderer is compiled once at startup.

## Removed (September 2026)

- `compileTailwind(overrideCss)` and the `pathland_tailwind_compile` binding are
  **deleted** — the renderer is inline-only now and needs no compiler. The demo
  `/tailwind.css` endpoints (`TailwindCssController` / `TailwindCssResource`)
  and the `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/tailwind.css">` in both `SessionApp`
  files are removed.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The Inter webfont is referenced by the `--pl-font-sans` token but not yet
  bundled (documented follow-up; falls back to `system-ui`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — JNA shim tests (skip when the Rust dylib
is absent); part of the non-demo reactor run on JDK 17.

cd /Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland && git commit -q -m "feat(render-html): inline-all styling + built-in design system; drop Tailwind

Revert the HTML renderer to pure inline styling (decision A) and replace
the Tailwind pipeline with our own tokenized design system:

- All opcode properties (alignment, text alignment/case, font style/design,
  underline/strikethrough, visible, clips-to-bounds, hit-testing, invert,
  truncation) now emit inline CSS in a single style attribute; 1 dp = 1 CSS px.
- New css::STYLE block injected into every document: vendored preflight reset
  (Tailwind CSS, MIT), :root design tokens (--pl-color-*/--pl-radius-*/
  --pl-font-sans/button tokens) named to match protocol design-token paths so
  SET_DESIGN_TOKEN can retheme, and .pathland-* component defaults including the
  prettified .pathland-button POC with prefers-color-scheme dark mode.
- Delete the entire Tailwind machinery: tw.rs, tailwind.rs, build.rs,
  scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs, the tailwind-embed feature, and the
  pathland_tailwind_compile C ABI.

Renderer remains stateless/streaming; tests updated to assert inline CSS." && git log --oneline -1
